items.title: New benchmark shows even advanced AI agents struggle with everyday tasks
items.description: TechCrunch reports that as millions embrace personal AI assistants, a new benchmark reveals even the most advanced AI models struggle to complete everyday tasks reliably and safely without introducing potential new problems.

items.title: Maple raises $5.3M for encrypted AI products designed to protect user data
items.description: TechCrunch reports that startup Maple raised $5.3 million to build AI products whose encrypted architecture is designed to prevent even the company itself from accessing users' private data.

items.title: Roboflow's Label by Example auto-labels images from a few of your own labeled examples
items.description: The Roboflow blog describes Label by Example, which shows an auto labeling model a few of the user's own labeled images so it follows the dataset's labeling rules without any training.

items.title: AI-assisted proof of Riemann hypothesis work appears solid but its meaning is unclear
items.description: Ars Technica reports on a new AI-assisted proof related to the Riemann hypothesis, noting that the proof seems solid but it is not yet clear what it tells mathematicians.

items.title: The Conversation explains what AI chips are and why Nvidia's graphics chips became central to AI.
items.description: The Conversation explains what AI chips are and how Nvidia, dominant in graphics chips by the early 2000s, found those chips well suited for running AI.

items.title: Databricks outlines data modeling best practices for an agentic customer data platform's data foundation.
items.description: The Databricks Blog presents data modeling best practices for an agentic customer data platform (CDP), Part 1 covering the data foundation, opening with a customer wishlist scenario.

items.title: BBC's Faisal Islam: fears over the AI boom persist despite Nvidia developments
items.description: BBC's Faisal Islam argues that legitimate fears about the AI boom existed before Huang's abrupt exit from Nvidia and that his return will not resolve them, per the excerpt.

items.title: WIRED: Jensen Huang apologizes to Nvidia staff in first all-hands since return
items.description: WIRED reports that Nvidia's CEO apologized to employees in his first all-hands since his return, discussing his personal life, defending his reinstatement, and acknowledging his management style had hurt staff.

items.title: Roboflow launches Cloud Streaming, a managed service for vision AI on live video
items.description: The Roboflow blog describes Cloud Streaming as a managed service for running vision AI on live video, connecting cameras via stream URL, local connector, RTMP, or phone, with Roboflow managing the GPUs.

items.title: The Register: AI coding agent, browser and Mac tool exposed a financial firm's access key in under 6 minutes
items.description: The Register reports that an AI coding agent, a browser, and a Mac tool found a financial firm's access key in under six minutes, with no sophisticated malware or attack framework required.

items.title: The Register: Microsoft refreshes Copilot app search for users without AI subscription
items.description: The Register reports Microsoft refreshed the Copilot app's search for users without an AI subscription, and notes Google's homepage demo leaves a familiar button out of the picture.

items.title: Simon Willison: GPT 6.2 Astra solves a historical mystery in 22 minutes
items.description: Simon Willison's blog relays history professor Mark Humphries' case study in which GPT-6.2 Astra, with minimal prompting, autonomously identified the creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook at Yale's Beinecke Library in 22 minutes using public sources.

items.title: The Register: Microsoft brings serverless PostgreSQL into Fabric to bridge transactions and analytics.
items.description: The Register reports Microsoft's HorizonDB preview brings serverless PostgreSQL into Fabric to bridge transactions and analytics, following rivals' moves, with analysts warning tighter integration could make an eventual exit harder.

items.title: MIT Technology Review: agentic AI is straining enterprise networks with surging traffic.
items.description: MIT Technology Review reports enterprise networks are under severe strain as AI deployment becomes the biggest source of network demand, with agentic AI tasks generating an estimated 450% more network traffic than the same tasks done by human workers.

items.title: Gradient Flow argues AI agents need a new data layer as agents begin making decisions.
items.description: The Gradient Flow post introduces the idea of an 'Agent Data Runtime,' arguing the data stack becomes less forgiving when AI agents make decisions, since stale records, inconsistent definitions, and incorrect permissions can cause operational failures rather than just bad reports.
